subtitle: Seven volumes, one engine: what each book is for, and the chapters planned for each
intro: Volumes I and II follow things that happened to people: wars, sieges, plagues and eruptions, with many eyes converging on the same days. From Volume III on, each book takes one theme, because each theme has its own shape. In exploration the convergence is an encounter between travellers and hosts. In discovery it is rival notebooks racing for the same result. In the arts it is friends and rivals in the same rooms. In great meetings it is many note-takers at one table. In transport it is the long arc from a first idea, through the trials that failed, to the day a new way of moving became ordinary.

Chapters marked 'in this book' are published here. The rest are leads chosen because the records are known to exist; none has been verified yet, and each will be researched and fact-checked the way the published chapters were.

parts.title: Volume III · Edges of the Map — exploration and encounter

chapters.title: The Treasure Fleets
chapters.premise: Zheng He's seven voyages, seen by the Chinese interpreters who sailed with them and by the courts and ports that received them.
eyes: Ma Huan, Fei Xin, Gong Zhen (Ming voyage accounts)
Zheng He's dated steles at Galle and Changle
Ming court annals; Niccolò de' Conti in the same ports

chapters.title: Embassies to Samarkand and Beijing
chapters.premise: A Castilian ambassador at Timur's court and a Timurid painter at the Ming court: the same empires seen from opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Narrow Road
chapters.premise: Bashō's crafted travel journal against his companion Sora's plain diary of the same journey, which quietly contradicts it.

chapters.title: Endeavour
chapters.premise: Cook's first voyage through the journals of Cook, Banks and Parkinson, with Tupaia's drawings and Māori and Aboriginal accounts flagged as later or indirect.
eyes: Sydney Parkinson; Tupaia; Te Horeta Te Taniwha (recalled later)

chapters.title: Humboldt's America
chapters.premise: Humboldt and Bonpland from the Orinoco to Chimborazo to Jefferson's Washington, met by creole scientists who wanted to join them.

chapters.title: The Corps of Discovery
chapters.premise: Six journal-keepers on the same days, a British trader at the Mandan villages, and Lakota winter counts as dated Indigenous records.
eyes: Lewis, Clark, Ordway, Gass, Floyd, Whitehouse

chapters.title: The Source of the Nile
chapters.premise: Burton and Speke as rivals with conflicting journals; the caravan leaders who made the journey possible seen through both.

chapters.title: Ujiji, 1871
chapters.premise: Livingstone's field diary, recovered by modern imaging and different from the edited version, against Stanley's diary and the Swahili and Arab traders at Ujiji.
chapters.caution: Built around an authenticity question: what Livingstone first wrote versus what was published.

chapters.title: Fram
chapters.premise: Nansen and Johansen's diaries of a winter alone together, with the ship's crew drifting on without them.

chapters.title: The North Pole Dispute
chapters.premise: Peary, Matthew Henson and Frederick Cook each claimed the Pole; the Inughuit who travelled with them told their own story later.

chapters.title: The Race to the South Pole
chapters.premise: Five nations on one continent in the same season: Scott, Amundsen, Bjaaland, Bowers and Wilson, and Nobu Shirase's Japanese expedition.

chapters.title: Everest
chapters.premise: Hunt, Hillary, Noyce and Lowe, with James Morris's coded dispatch; Tenzing's account was told later and is flagged.
eyes: Edmund Hillary, Wilfrid Noyce, George Lowe

chapters.title: The Telescope Turned Skyward
chapters.premise: Galileo, Thomas Harriot and Kepler, months apart, looking at the same Moon and Jupiter.

chapters.title: The Transits of Venus
chapters.premise: One planned event, observed from Siberia, Tahiti, Pennsylvania, Norway and the Indian Ocean.
eyes: Le Gentil; Maximilian Hell; David Rittenhouse

chapters.title: Dissection in Edo
chapters.premise: Japanese physicians test a Dutch anatomy book against a body and begin a translation that changed Japanese medicine.

chapters.title: Darwin and Wallace
chapters.premise: A letter from Ternate reaches Down House, and two naturalists' work is read together at the Linnean Society.

chapters.title: The Curies
chapters.premise: Becquerel's plates and the Curies' laboratory notebooks, still radioactive today.

chapters.title: Fission
chapters.premise: Hahn's results in Berlin and Meitner's interpretation in exile, worked out in letters.

chapters.title: The Double Helix
chapters.premise: Rosalind Franklin's notebooks set against the Cambridge race and the letters of the time.
eyes: Francis Crick (letter to his son, March 1953)
chapters.caution: Watson's account is a later memoir and will be flagged.

parts.title: Volume V · The Studio — artistic movements

chapters.title: Florence
chapters.premise: Landucci's diary, Savonarola's rise and fall, and the committee — Leonardo and Botticelli among them — that decided where Michelangelo's David would stand.

chapters.title: Grasmere
chapters.premise: Dorothy Wordsworth's journals beside the poems William and Coleridge drew from them.

chapters.title: The Ninth
chapters.premise: Beethoven's conversation books around the premiere — including entries his secretary later forged.
eyes: Beethoven's visitors in the conversation books

chapters.title: The First Impressionist Exhibition
chapters.premise: Morisot, Pissarro and Monet against the critics and the Goncourt journal.

chapters.title: Vienna 1900
chapters.premise: Schnitzler's daily diary, Alma Mahler's diaries and the city's cafés, Secession and clinics.

chapters.title: The Rite of Spring
chapters.premise: The premiere and the uproar, from the stalls and backstage.
eyes: Harry Kessler (diary; a Volume I eye)

chapters.title: The Bauhaus
chapters.premise: Oskar Schlemmer's diaries, Klee's teaching notes and Gropius's letters.

chapters.title: The Harlem Renaissance
chapters.premise: Alice Dunbar-Nelson's diary among the writers, salons and journals of Harlem.

parts.title: Volume VI · The Room — meetings of minds over critical issues

chapters.title: The Diet of Worms
chapters.premise: Luther before the emperor; the papal nuncio's dispatches; Dürer's diary lament when he believed Luther captured.
eyes: Albrecht Dürer (diary; a Volume II eye)

chapters.title: The House of Worship
chapters.premise: Akbar's debates between faiths, recorded by an admirer, a critic and the Jesuits in the hall.

chapters.title: Philadelphia
chapters.premise: The Constitutional Convention through several delegates' notes of the same debates.
eyes: Robert Yates, Rufus King, James McHenry

chapters.title: The Congress of Vienna
chapters.premise: Diplomats' diaries and the secret police's reports on the same delegates.

chapters.title: Seneca Falls
chapters.premise: The first women's rights convention, its declaration and the press.

chapters.title: Paris, 1919
chapters.premise: The peace conference through delegates of many nations, including the petitions of those left outside the room.
eyes: Faisal; the young Ho Chi Minh's petition

chapters.title: Yalta
chapters.premise: Three leaders, their interpreters, daughters and doctors.

chapters.title: Bandung
chapters.premise: Twenty-nine Asian and African nations meet; a novelist and the delegates write it down.

parts.title: Volume VII · Getting There — transportation, from first idea to mastery

chapters.title: Lighter Than Air
chapters.premise: The Montgolfiers' paper globe, the first people aloft, the hydrogen balloon over the Tuileries, and the Channel crossing — watched by Benjamin Franklin, who wrote it all home.
eyes: Jean-Pierre Blanchard and John Jeffries (Channel crossing, 1785)

chapters.title: Steam on the Water
chapters.premise: Fulton's Hudson run, then the 1838 Atlantic race between Sirius and Great Western.

chapters.title: Rainhill and After
chapters.premise: The locomotive trials, the actress who rode on the footplate with Stephenson, and the opening day that killed a minister.
eyes: George Stephenson; the Duke of Wellington's party

chapters.title: Joining the Oceans and the Continent
chapters.premise: The Suez Canal opens in November, six months after the Golden Spike in Utah; the guests, the engineers and the workers who are barely in the record.
eyes: Chinese workers (traced through company records, flagged)

chapters.title: The Road
chapters.premise: Bertha Benz's long drive, the bicycle craze, and the Peking-to-Paris race of 1907.

chapters.title: Kitty Hawk
chapters.premise: Lilienthal's gliders, Langley's failures on the Potomac, and the Wrights' diaries and telegram of 17 December 1903.
eyes: Kill Devil Hills lifesaving crew (John Daniels)

chapters.title: Across the Channel and the Atlantic
chapters.premise: Blériot's crossing, the first Atlantic flights, and Lindbergh's landing at Le Bourget.
eyes: Charles Lindbergh; the crowd at Le Bourget
chapters.caution: Lindbergh's later writing is copyrighted: digests only.

chapters.title: Airships
chapters.premise: Zeppelin's first flights, the Graf Zeppelin's world tour, and the end at Lakehurst.

chapters.title: Rockets
chapters.premise: Goddard's diary of the first liquid-fuel rocket, the rocket societies, and Sputnik's beep heard around the world.
eyes: Rocket-society members in Berlin and Moscow
chapters.caution: Links forward to Volume II's Apollo 11 chapter.

chapters.title: Faster Than Sound and the Jet Age
chapters.premise: The first supersonic flight, the Comet's triumph and failures, and Concorde's first flight.
eyes: de Havilland and accident inquiry records

chapters.title: The Bullet Train
chapters.premise: The Tōkaidō Shinkansen opens days before the Tokyo Olympics.

parts.title: Volume VIII · The Same Sky — one sky event, seen across the world

chapters.title: The Guest Star
chapters.premise: A new star bright enough to see by day, logged by the Song court, recalled in Japan and noted by an Arab physician; centuries later it became the Crab Nebula.

chapters.title: The Long-Haired Star
chapters.premise: Halley's Comet in the year of Hastings, from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and the Bayeux Tapestry to the Song and Goryeo star-watchers.

chapters.title: Halley's Eclipse
chapters.premise: The first eclipse mapped in advance, with the public asked to send in what they saw.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Fell
chapters.premise: A meteor storm over North America, from Yale to the Lakota winter counts.

chapters.title: The Carrington Storm
chapters.premise: A solar flare seen through a telescope, then aurorae to the tropics and telegraphs running on sky current.

chapters.title: Tunguska and the White Nights
chapters.premise: A blast over the Siberian taiga, recorded by herders, seismographs, barographs and bright nights across Europe.

chapters.title: Through the Tail
chapters.premise: Halley's Comet photographed worldwide, and the night Earth passed through its tail.

chapters.title: Light Bent
chapters.premise: Two expeditions to Brazil and Príncipe test Einstein's prediction during an eclipse.
